faq.q: What is the origin of Hamid?
faq.a: Hamid is associated with Arabic. Hamid is Arabic حَامِد (Ḥāmid) 'one who praises, praiser', the active participle of the root ح م د (ḥ-m-d). The source gloss 'praised, commendable' describes the passive participle; 'one who praises' is the sense of this form. Yes — the underlying form حامد is Arabic.

faq.q: What does Hamid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Hamid is rendered حامد and carries the sense قابلِ تعریف، محمود.

faq.q: What does Hamid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Hamid is rendered حامد and carries the sense ستوده، پسندیده.
A romanized syllable approximation is ha-mid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Hamid, hamid. Script forms are حامد, हामिद.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
